user.title: Home Desk
user.description: An issue tracker for your smart home, for the manager, the household and AI agents.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Home Desk is already set up.

init.title: Repairs
init.description: Home Desk opens a ticket for each Home Assistant repair, resolves it when Home Assistant clears the repair, and reopens it if the repair comes back. Turn this on or off in Home Desk's Settings page. Here you can skip noisy integrations.

data_description.repairs_ignored_domains: Integration domains (for example `hacs`) whose repairs should not become tickets. Useful for noisy ones.

get_guide.name: Get guide
get_guide.description: START HERE if you are an AI agent. Returns the usage guide for Home Desk: what it is, ticket fields and statuses, how to review, comment on, update and close tickets, and conventions to follow.

get_changelog.name: Get changelog
get_changelog.description: Return the installed Home Desk version and its changelog: what changed, and any **Action:** or **Breaking:** notes. Pass `since` (the last version you reviewed) to get only newer releases. Call after Home Desk is updated.

since.name: Since version
since.description: Only include releases newer than this version. The Unreleased section is always included.

list_labels.name: List labels
list_labels.description: Return every label with its id, name, colour, description and how many tickets use it. Prefer an existing label over inventing a new one; a label name you use that doesn't exist is created automatically. Built-in labels: Bug, Enhancement, Task, Question, History and Blocked. (What part of the home a ticket is about is a category, see list_categories.)

create_label.name: Create label
create_label.description: Create a label, for example Zigbee or Needs review. Check list_labels first so you don't add a near-duplicate. Pass `actor` with your own name.

color.name: Colour
color.description: One of Home Assistant's colour names, e.g. teal. Picked automatically if left out.

icon.name: Icon
icon.description: An optional icon such as mdi:zigbee.

actor.name: Actor
actor.description: Who is acting, recorded on the timeline. AI agents: pass your own name (e.g. claude), otherwise the token owner's name is recorded.

update_label.name: Update label
update_label.description: Rename a label or change its colour, icon or description. Tickets keep the label when it is renamed. The built-in labels (Bug, Enhancement, Task, Question, History, Blocked) can't be changed.

color.name: Colour
color.description: A new colour name, e.g. teal.

icon.name: Icon
icon.description: A new icon such as mdi:zigbee.

actor.name: Actor
actor.description: Who is acting, recorded on the timeline. AI agents: pass your own name (e.g. claude), otherwise the token owner's name is recorded.

delete_label.name: Delete label
delete_label.description: Delete a label that no ticket uses. A label in use is refused: remove it from those tickets first, or ask the manager to delete it in the panel. The built-in labels can't be deleted.

actor.name: Actor
actor.description: Who is acting, recorded on the timeline. AI agents: pass your own name (e.g. claude), otherwise the token owner's name is recorded.

list_categories.name: List categories
list_categories.description: Return every category with its id, name, icon and how many tickets use it. A category says what part of the smart home a ticket is about (Home Assistant, Network, Lighting...). A ticket has at most one. Home Assistant is built in.

create_category.name: Create category
create_category.description: Create a category, for example Network or Cameras. Check list_categories first. Pass `actor` with your own name.

icon.name: Icon
icon.description: An optional icon such as mdi:lan.

actor.name: Actor
actor.description: Who is acting, recorded on the timeline. AI agents: pass your own name (e.g. claude), otherwise the token owner's name is recorded.

update_category.name: Update category
update_category.description: Rename a category or change its icon. The built-in Home Assistant category can't be changed.

icon.name: Icon
icon.description: A new icon such as mdi:lan.

actor.name: Actor
actor.description: Who is acting, recorded on the timeline. AI agents: pass your own name (e.g. claude), otherwise the token owner's name is recorded.

delete_category.name: Delete category
delete_category.description: Delete a category that no ticket uses. A category in use is refused: move its tickets first, or ask the manager to delete it in the panel. The built-in Home Assistant category can't be deleted.

actor.name: Actor
actor.description: Who is acting, recorded on the timeline. AI agents: pass your own name (e.g. claude), otherwise the token owner's name is recorded.

get_stats.name: Get stats
get_stats.description: Return ticket counts by status, urgent, unassigned and with-AI-agent counts, how many active tickets have no category, and every label and category (with counts). A good first call to see what needs attention.

list_tickets.name: List tickets
list_tickets.description: List ticket summaries (no bodies); use get_ticket for the full ticket. Defaults to active tickets, excluding those labelled History. Label `needs-review` marks tickets whose state has not been verified yet.

status.name: Status
status.description: A status, a comma-separated list, `active` (new and in_progress; the default) or `all`.

query.name: Query
query.description: Search text across title, description, comments, resolution, labels and entities.

requester.name: Requester
requester.description: Only tickets raised by this person.

label.name: Label
label.description: Only tickets with this label (name or id), e.g. Bug, Enhancement or Blocked.

category.name: Category
category.description: Only tickets in this category (name or id), or `none` for tickets with no category yet.

include_history.name: Include history
include_history.description: Include tickets labelled History (records of past work). Default false.

run_state.name: Run state
run_state.description: Only tickets whose AI Agent run is in this state, or a comma-separated list: requested, running, proposed, approved, done, failed, stopped, dismissed. The runner polls for `requested` and `approved`.

raise_issue.name: Raise issue
raise_issue.description: For automations: open a ticket for a problem, once, however often it is reported. The key says which problem it is. Nothing open for the key: a ticket is created. One already open: nothing happens (or one comment an hour with `on_existing: comment`), and a higher priority is taken over. A resolved ticket for the key is reopened. The ticket says which automation or script raised it. Returns `result` (created, found, reopened or commented) and the ticket. Pair it with clear_issue.

key.name: Key
key.description: A short name for the problem, the same every time it is reported, e.g. soil-probe-garden-dry. Trimmed and lower-cased, at most 80 characters. It never touches tickets made from Home Assistant Repairs.

description.name: Description
description.description: Details in markdown. Used as the comment when an open ticket is raised again with `on_existing: comment`, and when a resolved one reopens.

priority.name: Priority
priority.description: low, normal, high or urgent. An open ticket only ever goes up.

on_existing.name: If already open
on_existing.description: ignore (the default) does nothing; comment adds a comment, at most once an hour for each key.

labels.name: Labels
labels.description: Label names or ids. Names that don't exist yet are created.

category.name: Category
category.description: What part of the home this is about (see list_categories). It must already exist.

entities.name: Entities
entities.description: Home Assistant entity ids this ticket concerns.

devices.name: Devices
devices.description: Home Assistant device ids this ticket concerns.

areas.name: Areas
areas.description: Home Assistant area ids this ticket concerns.

actor.name: Actor
actor.description: Who is acting, recorded on the timeline. AI agents: pass your own name (e.g. claude), otherwise the token owner's name is recorded.

clear_issue.name: Clear issue
clear_issue.description: For automations: the problem raised with raise_issue is over. Resolves the open ticket for the key with a note. If no ticket is open for the key, nothing happens and it is not an error. Returns `result` (cleared or none).

resolution.name: Resolution
resolution.description: What to record. A default note is used if left out.

actor.name: Actor
actor.description: Who is acting, recorded on the timeline. AI agents: pass your own name (e.g. claude), otherwise the token owner's name is recorded.

get_ticket.name: Get ticket
get_ticket.description: Return one ticket in full: description, resolution, labels, entities, timeline of comments and changes, and related tickets.

create_ticket.name: Create ticket
create_ticket.description: Create a ticket and return it. Search first (list_tickets with a query) to avoid duplicates. AI agents: call get_guide first and pass `actor` with your own name.

title.name: Title
title.description: Short summary of the problem, request or idea.

description.name: Description
description.description: Details in markdown: what happened, evidence, what was expected.

priority.name: Priority
priority.description: low, normal, high or urgent (urgent = safety, security or whole-house outage).

requester.name: Requester
requester.description: Who raised it. Defaults to the actor.

assignee.name: Assignee
assignee.description: Who is working on it. Leave empty for unassigned. Assigning a ticket to an AI agent (name starting `ai:`) hands it to that agent; a `home_desk_event` of kind `assigned` is fired.

labels.name: Labels
labels.description: Label names or ids, e.g. Bug, Enhancement, Task, Question. Names that don't exist yet are created.

category.name: Category
category.description: What part of the home this is about (see list_categories), e.g. Network. It must already exist: create_category first if it is new. Leave empty if unsure.

entities.name: Entities
entities.description: Home Assistant entity ids this ticket concerns. People can click through to them.

devices.name: Devices
devices.description: Home Assistant device ids (from the device registry) this ticket concerns; the AI agent looks at all of a device's entities.

areas.name: Areas
areas.description: Home Assistant area ids this ticket concerns, when it is about a place rather than one thing.

actor.name: Actor
actor.description: Who is acting, recorded on the timeline. AI agents: pass your own name (e.g. claude), otherwise the token owner's name is recorded.

update_ticket.name: Update ticket
update_ticket.description: Change a ticket's fields. Pass only what should change; every change is logged on the timeline. To close a ticket use close_ticket so a resolution is recorded.

status.name: Status
status.description: new, in_progress, resolved or closed. A ticket moves from new to in_progress by itself the first time anyone acts on it, and a resolved ticket closes by itself after the delay in Settings, so you rarely need this. To mark a ticket as waiting on something, add the Blocked label. (`open` is accepted and means in_progress.)

assignee.name: Assignee
assignee.description: New assignee; empty to unassign. When an AI agent a ticket is assigned to comments on it, the ticket is handed back (the assignee is cleared) automatically.

labels.name: Labels
labels.description: Replace all labels with this list.

category.name: Category
category.description: Move the ticket to this category (name or id, from list_categories); empty to clear.

add_labels.name: Add labels
add_labels.description: Label names or ids to add. Unknown names are created.

remove_labels.name: Remove labels
remove_labels.description: Label names or ids to remove.

actor.name: Actor
actor.description: Who is acting, recorded on the timeline. AI agents: pass your own name (e.g. claude), otherwise the token owner's name is recorded.

add_comment.name: Add comment
add_comment.description: Add a comment to a ticket's timeline. Use it to record findings: what you checked, what you found, with times and values.

internal.name: Internal note
internal.description: True makes a private note that the requester can't see.

keep_assigned.name: Keep assigned
keep_assigned.description: True leaves the ticket queued for the AI agent after this comment instead of handing it back to the manager, for evidence on a ticket the agent is meant to keep watching. Default false: an agent's comment hands the ticket back.

actor.name: Actor
actor.description: Who is acting, recorded on the timeline. AI agents: pass your own name (e.g. claude), otherwise the token owner's name is recorded.

claim_run.name: Claim run
claim_run.description: Experimental, for a runner that is not part of the first release. The runner takes a run that a person asked for (Run AI Agent Now, a read-only review) or approved (Proceed, the change). Only one runner can take it; a second call fails. Pass `actor` with the runner's name.

actor.name: Actor
actor.description: Who is acting, recorded on the timeline. AI agents: pass your own name (e.g. claude), otherwise the token owner's name is recorded.

note_run.name: Note run
note_run.description: Experimental, for a runner that is not part of the first release. The runner says what it is doing right now, shown in the ticket's working indicator (for example "Using get_ticket"). Only while it is running the ticket. Pass `actor` with the runner's name.

note.name: Note
note.description: A few words about the current step, at most 120 characters.

actor.name: Actor
actor.description: Who is acting, recorded on the timeline. AI agents: pass your own name (e.g. claude), otherwise the token owner's name is recorded.

finish_run.name: Finish run
finish_run.description: Experimental, for a runner that is not part of the first release. The runner reports back on a claimed run, as a comment from the agent. `proposed`: what it found and what it would change, which waits for a person to press Proceed. `done`: the approved change was made. `failed`: why it could not. Fails if the run was stopped.

body.name: Comment
body.description: What it found and would change, what it did, or why it failed, in markdown.

actor.name: Actor
actor.description: Who is acting, recorded on the timeline. AI agents: pass your own name (e.g. claude), otherwise the token owner's name is recorded.

close_ticket.name: Close ticket
close_ticket.description: Resolve or close a ticket with resolution notes (the cause and the fix). Only close when you are confident; otherwise comment and leave it open.

resolution.name: Resolution
resolution.description: What the cause was and what fixed it.

status.name: Status
status.description: `resolved` (fixed; the default) or `closed` (won't fix, superseded or no longer relevant).

actor.name: Actor
actor.description: Who is acting, recorded on the timeline. AI agents: pass your own name (e.g. claude), otherwise the token owner's name is recorded.

link_tickets.name: Link tickets
link_tickets.description: Mark two tickets as related; shown on both.

actor.name: Actor
actor.description: Who is acting, recorded on the timeline. AI agents: pass your own name (e.g. claude), otherwise the token owner's name is recorded.

merge_tickets.name: Merge tickets
merge_tickets.description: Fold duplicate tickets into one. `ticket_id` is the ticket to keep; the tickets in `merge_ids` have their comments, description, labels, files and linked repairs moved onto it and are closed as merged. Do this for tickets that are really the same problem; it can't be undone.

ticket_id.name: Ticket to keep
ticket_id.description: The ticket the others are merged into.

merge_ids.name: Tickets to merge
merge_ids.description: Numbers of the tickets to fold in, e.g. [12, 15].

actor.name: Actor
actor.description: Who is acting, recorded on the timeline. AI agents: pass your own name (e.g. claude), otherwise the token owner's name is recorded.
